newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 16.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Tony Blair will appeal to the Labour party to end its squabbling in a speech to a business audience at the Guildhall tonight, warning that continued division could ruin Labour's chances in the coming general election.
CITY READY FOR EMU SAYS BANK GOVERNOR

Eddie George, the Governor of the Bank of England, said today that the City was well-placed to benefit from the drive towards monetary union, whether Britain decides to join EMU or not. George commented that Britain would be correct to stay outside the single currency for the time being, citing high unemployment in France as potential for serious problems.
BRITISH GAS STEPS UP ROW OVER COSTS
British Gas is calling on Ofgas to double the 40 million stg budget it has allowed the company for restructuring in its latest price cutting recommendations.
BORAL SAYS GOODBYE TO BRITAIN WITH FOUR MLN STG SALE

Boral, the Australian building materials giant, has completed its withdrawal from the British market with the sale today of its construction materials arm. Pozzolanic Lytag was sold to The Rugby Group for four million stg.
HIVE-OFFS "NET 8.8 BILLION STG A YEAR FOR STATE'

A study by the National Economic Research Associates for the Conservative Party's Centre for Policy Studies has found that the privatisation programme has been of huge financial benefit to government and taxpayers. The 33 companies privatised between 1984 and 1991 contributed on average 8.8 billion stg to the Exchequer per year between 1987 and 1995, the largest part of which was corporation tax.
AIDS DRUG FILIP IN PIPELINE AT GLAXO
Glaxo Wellcome is today expected to release encouraging early results of a new Aids drug, one of the pipeline products which the company is hoping will counteract falling sales of Zantac.
